Condition (45) follows automatically from formulation (44): if φ(a) = s ∈ S'', then φ(σa) = σ_G(s) = s, so f_S(o(a)) = s = f_S(o(σa)). It must, however, be imposed in the (f_S, B̃', B̃'→Ã'') and subgraph formulations. Grothendieck caught this in a marginal addition.

The subgraph reformulation ('a subgraph G_{B̃'} plus a morphism G_{B̃'} → G'') is not equivalent unless condition (45) is added there too. A morphism from the subgraph forgets that the endpoints of deleted arcs must be identified.

Generalized morphisms as defined need not be surjective on vertices or bijective on non-contracted arcs. So they are much more general than contractions. This is harmless, since the MD-graph conditions on the next page restrict them.

missed.claim: An explicit unpublished construction of the category of stable dual graphs with contraction morphisms. Arcs may map to vertices, and maps commute with an involution that is extended by the identity on vertices. This anticipates the formalism of modular operads (Getzler–Kapranov) and Borisov–Manin's graph categories, which are usually dated to the 1990s–2000s.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck had the now-standard combinatorial category indexing the boundary of \bar M_{g,n}, with a clean S ⊔ Ã encoding, well before it entered the literature. The mathematics itself is now routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct, but essentially standard formalization of edge-contraction morphisms of dual graphs. It is historically interesting as an early unpublished precursor of the stable-graph category of modular operads, but would not surprise a specialist mathematically.
